source.title: WRC Digest (June 2023)
source.content:
Dear WCA Community,

The first half of 2023 was quite productive for the WCA Regulations Committee. The number of competitions, as well as the number of incidents, has increased. Here you have the most notable of the recent incidents:

1. After a competitor finished their average, the scrambles were double checked, and it was found that one of the solves was misscrambled only by one move, affecting only the last move of the solve. The WCA Delegates provided an extra attempt, and the WRC later agreed that although the misscramble was the same in difficulty and the solve was only different by one last move, the extra attempt should be used, as always done with misscrambles when the extra is available. See the Incident Log entry [here](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/86).
2. After a competition, several attempts of high-profile competitors were found to be misscrambled. The WRC investigated each of those attempts to determine if they should stay based on the following criteria:
  * If the misscramble gives the competitor a significant advantage, the attempt should be changed to DNF.
  * If the misscramble is similar in difficulty to the original scramble, the attempt should be left as is.
  * If the misscramble cannot be analyzed (e.g. the video of the attempt is not available), the attempt should be left as is.  
See the Incident Log entry [here](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/87).
3. After a competition, several misscrambles were found to be sent out during certain events. As the number of misscrambles was significant, the WRC agreed to remove the results of the affected rounds. See the Incident Log entry [here](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/88).
4. After a competition, a competitor reported that they had both the scrambles from the previous group and from their (current) group in their average. The WCA Delegate also confirmed they could have left two consecutive scramble sets open at the same time. Since the scramble secrecy was violated, the WRC agreed that the results from the affected round should be removed (also resulting in the removal of the final round). See the Incident Log entry [here](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/89).
5. A competitor emailed the WRC reporting that some covers at this competition were translucent, attaching a picture proving that the scramble can be seen when the puzzle is under the cover under some angle. The WCA Delegates responded that they made sure translucent covers were double stacked in order to make them opaque enough. WRC reviewed the video evidence from the public resources and agreed that the results should be kept. See the Incident Log entry [here](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/90).
6. During inspection, a competitor reported that their timer was in a 4-pad mode. As later discovered, the competitor touched their camera during the inspection violating [Regulation 2i2b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2i2b), before reporting the timer issue. The WCA Delegates granted a provisional extra attempt, but the WRC agreed to keep a DNF since the competitor touched the camera before spotting the issue with the timer. See the Incident Log entry [here](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/91).

As most of the incidents that affected a significant amount of attempts were related to scramble concerns, the WRC would like to remind everyone (WCA Delegates, organizers and competitors) about the importance of this matter. All competitions must follow the [WCA Scramble Accountability Policy](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/documents/policies/external/Scramble%20Accountability.pdf) to avoid detrimental consequences for the competitors.

translation.title: WCA 规则委员会工作简报（2023 年 6 月）
translation.content:
各位 WCA 社区成员：

2023 年上半年，WCA 规则委员会完成了不少工作。比赛数量增加，相关事件也随之增多。以下是近期较值得关注的案例：

1. 一位选手完成全部还原后，复核打乱时发现其中一次仅有一步打乱错误，且只影响还原的最后一步。WCA 代表给予补赛，WRC 随后同意：虽然错误打乱的难度相同、还原只差最后一步，但既然有补赛，就应与通常的错误打乱处理一致，采用补赛成绩。事件记录见[此处](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/86)。
2. 一场比赛结束后，发现几位知名选手的多次还原使用了错误打乱。WRC 逐次调查，并根据以下标准决定是否保留：
   * 如果错误打乱给选手带来明显优势，成绩应改为 DNF。
   * 如果错误打乱与原打乱难度相近，成绩应保留。
   * 如果无法分析错误打乱，例如没有还原视频，成绩应保留。
   
   事件记录见[此处](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/87)。
3. 一场比赛结束后，发现某些项目多次发出了错误打乱。由于数量较多，WRC 同意删除受影响轮次的成绩。事件记录见[此处](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/88)。
4. 一场比赛结束后，一位选手反映，自己的几次还原混用了前一组和本组的打乱。WCA 代表也确认，自己可能同时打开了连续两组的打乱。由于打乱保密受到破坏，WRC 同意删除受影响轮次的成绩，因此决赛成绩也一并删除。事件记录见[此处](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/89)。
5. 一位选手发邮件向 WRC 反映，该场比赛使用的部分遮盖物半透明，并附图证明从某些角度可以看到罩内魔方的打乱状态。WCA 代表回复称，他们已确保将半透明遮盖物叠放两层，使其足够不透明。WRC 审查公开渠道的视频证据后，同意保留成绩。事件记录见[此处](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/90)。
6. 一位选手在观察期间反映计时器处于四触点模式。后来发现，在报告计时器问题之前，选手已在观察期间触碰摄像机，违反了[规则 2i2b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2i2b)。WCA 代表给予了临时补赛，但 WRC 认为选手在发现计时器问题前已触碰摄像机，因此应保留 DNF。事件记录见[此处](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/91)。

大多数影响大量成绩的事件都与打乱有关，因此 WRC 希望提醒所有 WCA 代表、组织者和选手重视这一问题。所有比赛都必须遵守 [WCA 打乱问责政策](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/documents/policies/external/Scramble%20Accountability.pdf)，避免给选手造成不利后果。
